title: Circuit valve escort and soft-handoff telemetry hotfix
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Fix: introduce staged 'circuit valve escort' to reduce flip-flop during ephemeral heartbeat storms; add telemetry and runtime flag; safe default config and canary rollout guidance.
body: Background: a production regression was observed where short-lived heartbeat jitter caused repeated circuit reopen/close cycles for a subset of regional nodes. That churn triggered unnecessary failovers and elevated p50/p95 latencies for affected tenants. Motivation: we need a minimal, conservative mitigation that reduces circuit flip-flop without changing SLO targets or doing broad tenant demotions. Summary: this PR introduces a lightweight 'circuit valve escort' (a staged soft-handoff layer) that biases reopens to prefer keeping a graceful degraded path open for a short escort window, emits telemetry for every escorted transition, and adds a runtime feature flag and conservative defaults so behavior is opt-in for canary during rollout. The change surface is intentionally small: a single coordinator shim, new metrics, gating tests, and a hotfix to the admission gate to avoid churn when KV-cache warmups are in progress. Checklist: - [x] Reproduced failure locally with synthetic heartbeat jitter harness - [x] Added unit tests for escort window edge cases - [x] End-to-end canary in eu-west-1 with 5% traffic for 6 hours - [x] Telemetry validated in staging (new metric names below) - [x] Rollout plan added in this PR description Implementation notes: - Escort window defaults to 250ms (configurable via runtime flag circuit.valve.escort_ms) - Escort logic: when a circuit is about to reopen, we check recent reopen count and active connection tail; if within thresholds we keep a soft-route open and mark the transition as 'escorted' rather than immediate reopen. This prevents rapid reopen-close cycles and preserves KV cache for short-lived retries. - Telemetry: emitted metrics: circuit_escort_count, circuit_escort_duration_ms, circuit_escort_outcome{kept|released}, circuit_escort_decision_reason_tag - Logs: sparse single-line debug when escort decision happens; guarded by rate-limiter. - Admission gate fix: admission gate previously accepted connections while KV cache was still warming, which contributed to churn. We now stall acceptance for 50ms if kv_warmup_inflight > 0 and tag the connection origin metric. Migration & safety: default flag is OFF for existing fleets; can be enabled via feature gate for canary clusters. No data migration required. Related: ENG-2141, SUP-342.
commits: fc1a2b3: add circuit valve escort coordinator and basic escort state machine
b2d3c4e: telemetry: register circuit_escort_* metrics and schema
c3e4f5a: admission gate: delay new accepts during kv warmup (50ms guard)
d4f5a6b: tests: unit + integration harness for heartbeat jitter and escort window
e5a6b7c: docs: feature gate and rollout instructions in ops/runbooks.md
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Concerned about default window size. 250ms might be too long for low-latency tenants — can we make this per-tenant configurable and document tradeoffs?

Maya Chen: Answered: exposed runtime flag circuit.valve.escort_ms and added per-tenant override hooks on dedicated clusters; docs updated to explain tradeoffs. Kept 250ms as conservative canary default to reduce churn observed in staging.
Evelyn Soto: Please add a metric for number of 'escorts prevented reopen' so we can measure suppressed flaps.
Maya Chen: Added circuit_escort_outcome and increment points for 'kept' path. Also added a short sampling log line for RCA if needed.
Luca Moretti: Can the admission gate 50ms stall cause connection starvation under heavy burst? Suggest rate-limiting or backoff.
Maya Chen: We limit stalls to when kv_warmup_inflight > 0 and added backoff counters; also added a safety circuit that falls back to immediate accept after 3 stalls to avoid starvation.
tests_summary: Unit coverage: +8% on coordinator package; added edge-case tests for escort timeouts
Integration: heartbeat jitter harness reproduces flips pre-fix and stable post-fix
Staging canary: 5% traffic in eu-west-1 for 6 hours showed 78% reduction in circuit flip events for affected cohort
merge_commit_message: squash: circuit valve escort + admission gate kv warmup stall; add telemetry and runbook
notes: Canary rollout plan: enable feature gate in eu-west-1 for 24h; if metrics look stable, progressive rollout to NA regions over 48-72h. Monitor: circuit_escort_outcome, circuit_open_count, regional_failover_count. Ops runbook updated with rollback steps (disable flag + revert).
